newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GIO sees better performance in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GIO sees better performance in 96/97.

text.p: Insurance company GIO Australia Ltd said on Tuesday it saw an improved performance from its general insurance and managed investment activities and a positive outlook for the investment and reinsurance markets in the year to June 30, 1997.

"Lending activities should also contribute to improved performance, with more favourable economic conditions likely to increase demand for loan products and operational initiatives to improve GIO's competitive position and profit potential," GIO said in a statement.
GIO earlier said its net profit after the transfer of funds to its disaster reserve rose 1.1 percent to A$142.2 million.

The insurance company said significant changes were underway to the way in which it distributed and serviced its personal general insurance business in order to improve the profitability of that business and provide a better service to its customers.
"The benefits of the restructuring should begin to emerge in 1996/97, with the full effects to become apparent in 1997/98," the company said.
GIO said it saw better economic conditions over the year but growth was seen at a lower pace than in the past three years.

"The prospect of a protracted period of modest economic growth and low inflation provides a favourable background for domestic interest rates to decline. However, an increase in world economic growth rates over the next year may push global interest rates higher, limiting the scope for Australian rates to fall," the company said.
GIO said its property portfolio had a relatively high exposure to the Sydney central business district and was expected to benefit from rising rents as the demand for office space increased.
"Investor confidence has improved, with the prospect of a significant reduction in the Commonwealth budget deficit over the coming year, enhancing the scope for lower interest rates," GIO said.
The insurance group said it saw scope fo improvement in corporate earnings and strong returns from the Australian sharemarket in the medium term.
GIO said despite an easing in prices for both property catastrophe and liability business, the reinsurance outlook remained reasonably positive with no signs yet of a dramatic decline in prices.
"Conditions are also softer in the corporate insurance market and GIO Insurance will maintain a selective approach to underwriting," the company said.

GIO said a new group subsidiary, GIO Asset Management (Asia) Sdn Bhd was being established in Malaysia to assist with the management of the group's growing pool of investment assets in the region. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
